question: What is the primary purpose of a research study design?

options.A: To act as a structural blueprint for the research project
options.B: To calculate the exact budget needed for laboratory tests
options.C: To determine the final statistical software to purchase
options.D: To list the names of all participating clinical midwives

explanation: The study design guides the overall direction of the study, similar to how an architectural blueprint guides construction. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h1)

question: When should a researcher choose a qualitative design over a quantitative one?

options.A: When calculating the statistical prevalence of malaria in pregnancy
options.B: When measuring exact medication dosages and blood pressure levels
options.C: When comparing birth weights across three different hospitals
options.D: When exploring deep human experiences and personal feelings

explanation: Qualitative designs focus on understanding human perspectives, opinions, and lived experiences rather than numerical measurements. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h1)

question: What do inclusion criteria define in a research methodology?

options.A: Standard laboratory tests required for every recruited patient
options.B: Financial incentives given to women attending antenatal care
options.C: Reasons why a participant should be dropped after analysis
options.D: Characteristics a participant must possess to join the study

explanation: Inclusion criteria set the baseline requirements that every potential participant must meet to be considered for the research. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h2)

question: A researcher is studying postnatal depression among teenage mothers in a general hospital. Which of these would serve as an exclusion criterion?

options.A: A teenage mother experiencing severe depressive symptoms
options.B: A primigravida teenager delivering her first baby at home
options.C: A teenage mother who willingly signs the consent form
options.D: An adult mother aged 35 years seeking postnatal care

explanation: Adult mothers fall outside the specific age bracket defined by the study objective and would therefore be excluded. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which sampling method gives every member of the target population an equal chance of being chosen?
explanation: Probability sampling relies on random selection, ensuring every individual has a known, non-zero probability of inclusion. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why would a researcher choose stratified sampling over simple random sampling?

options.A: To reduce the final calculated sample size to the smallest possible number
options.B: To avoid having to list all members of the accessible population
options.C: To completely eliminate all forms of human error during data entry
options.D: To guarantee that specific subgroups are fairly represented in the sample

explanation: Stratification divides the population into meaningful groups and samples from each, ensuring minority or specific categories are not missed. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a pilot test on a research questionnaire?

options.A: To identify and fix confusing questions before the main study
options.B: To train hospital management on how to write research proposals
options.C: To collect all the required data without needing a large sample
options.D: To complete the final data analysis and publish the findings early

explanation: Pilot testing reveals flaws in instrument design so researchers can refine items before committing time and resources to the main study. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h4)

question: What does instrument reliability guarantee in research measurements?

options.A: That repeated measurements will yield consistent results
options.B: That participants will answer every single question honestly
options.C: That the sample size is large enough for statistical testing
options.D: That the questions accurately measure the intended clinical concept

explanation: Reliability is all about consistency and stability over multiple administrations or observations. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a data collection protocol?

options.A: To calculate the exact monetary budget required for printing forms
options.B: To provide medical treatment directly to emergency obstetric patients
options.C: To serve as a step-by-step operational manual for gathering information
options.D: To replace the need for ethical approval from hospital management

explanation: A protocol standardizes the research process so every team member collects data in the exact same manner. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is standardizing data collection across multiple research assistants especially important in a busy hospital?

options.A: It minimizes human error and variations in how data are recorded
options.B: It eliminates the need for any statistical software analysis
options.C: It automatically increases the final sample size calculation
options.D: It ensures that patients never experience long waiting times

explanation: When multiple people collect data, standardization ensures personal interviewing styles or recording habits do not skew the results. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h5)

question: What principle of research ethics is demonstrated when a patient freely agrees to participate after being fully informed?
explanation: Autonomy respects a person's right to self-determination, exercised through voluntary informed consent. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard procedure for maintaining data quality during implementation?

options.A: Throwing away original raw data sheets before final analysis
options.B: Supervising research assistants during clinical data gathering
options.C: Cross-checking digital data entries against original paper logs
options.D: Regularly auditing filled questionnaires for missing entries

explanation: Discarding original raw data destroys your audit trail and violates good research governance. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T3#BMP314_U1_T3_h6)
